result:
No — this warrants at least one other human's sign-off before merging, not a self-approval, and skipping review is the wrong tradeoff here.

The diff being one line doesn't make the risk small: `ENFORCE_MFA_FOR_ADMINS` is a shared flag across all backend services, so flipping it removes MFA for every admin account, everywhere, for however long it's actually live — not just the one admin who's locked out. "Revert within the hour" is a plan, not a guarantee (deploy fails, reviewer gets pulled away, second deploy has an unrelated issue) — the whole point of a second reviewer here is that they might catch the blast-radius problem you're describing and suggest a better fix, like resetting/reprovisioning MFA for just that one admin account (recovery codes, admin panel MFA reset) instead of disabling enforcement globally.

If a scoped per-user fix genuinely isn't available and the global flag is the only option, get a quick real approval from someone else (even a fast Slack thumbs-up counts) rather than self-approving, and have a specific person explicitly own flipping it back — don't rely on "someone will remember."
